- [Road Base Material Supplier in Goa | GSB & WMM](https://www.omgroupco.com/products/road-base-material): OM GROUP supplies road construction materials across Goa, including GSB, WMM aggregate and graded aggregates for infrastructure. Request a quote.

  Q: What is road base material?
  A: Road base material is a broad construction term for graded granular materials used in the base or sub-base layers of a road pavement. Depending on the project specification, it may refer to GSB, WMM or another specified graded aggregate.

  Q: Is road base material one specific product?
  A: No. It is a category term, not one manufactured product. The specific material required depends on the pavement layer and the project's specification.

  Q: What determines which road base material a project needs?
  A: The pavement layer being constructed (sub-base or base course) and the project's contract specification together determine whether GSB, WMM or another graded aggregate applies.

  Q: What is the difference between road base material and GSB?
  A: "Road base material" is a broad category term; GSB is one specific, defined material within it, governed by MoRTH Clause 401 and used at the sub-base position.

  Q: What is the difference between road base material and WMM?
  A: "Road base material" is the broad category; WMM is one specific material within it, governed by MoRTH Clause 406 and used as the base course above GSB.

  Q: Is GSB a road base material?
  A: Yes — GSB is the granular sub-base layer, one of the specific materials the broader term "road base material" can refer to.

  Q: What is GSB?
  A: GSB (Granular Sub-Base) is a graded granular material placed and compacted over prepared subgrade to form the sub-base layer of a road pavement. Full detail is on the GSB page.

  Q: What is MoRTH Clause 401?
  A: MoRTH Clause 401 is the principal Indian reference governing Granular Sub-Base material, grading and construction requirements.

  Q: Where is GSB used in a pavement?
  A: GSB is generally used as the sub-base layer, above the subgrade and below the base course (typically WMM).

  Q: Does OM Group supply GSB?
  A: Yes. OM Group supplies GSB across Goa — see the GSB page for grading, testing and specification detail.

  Q: Is WMM a road base material?
  A: Yes — WMM is the base-course material above GSB, also within the broader "road base material" category.

  Q: What is WMM?
  A: WMM (Wet Mix Macadam) is a pavement base-course material made by mixing clean, crushed, graded aggregate with controlled water and compacting it, per MoRTH Clause 406. Full detail is on the WMM page.

  Q: What is MoRTH Clause 406?
  A: MoRTH Clause 406 is the principal Indian reference governing Wet Mix Macadam production, grading and construction requirements.

  Q: Where is WMM used in a pavement?
  A: WMM is generally used as the base course, above the granular sub-base and below the bituminous or surface layer.

  Q: Does OM Group supply aggregate for WMM?
  A: Yes. OM Group supplies the crushed, graded aggregate fractions used in WMM production — see the WMM page for the full aggregate-supply detail.

  Q: What is the difference between GSB and WMM?
  A: GSB is the sub-base layer, governed by MoRTH Clause 401; WMM is the base course above it, governed by Clause 406, more rigorously graded and plant-mixed with controlled moisture. They are not interchangeable.

  Q: Can WMM replace GSB?
  A: No, not without engineering/specification approval — GSB and WMM serve different pavement positions with different grading and physical requirements.

  Q: Can GSB replace WMM?
  A: No, for the same reason — the two materials occupy different, specified positions in the pavement structure.

  Q: Is crusher-run the same as road base material?
  A: Not automatically. Crusher-run is an uncontrolled mixed-size crusher output; it must be blended to a specified grading (GSB's or WMM's) before it meets either specification.

  Q: What is road metal?
  A: "Road metal" is a term with genuine regional and historical variation in Indian construction trade usage — it is not automatically equivalent to GSB or WMM.

  Q: Is recycled aggregate used as road base material?
  A: Recycled aggregate is used in some jurisdictions and project specifications, where the applicable specification explicitly permits it. It is neither promoted nor dismissed here — acceptance is project- and specification-specific.

  Q: What material is used below WMM?
  A: GSB (Granular Sub-Base) is generally used below WMM, forming the sub-base layer beneath the WMM base course.

  Q: What is used as a road sub-base?
  A: GSB, governed by MoRTH Clause 401, is the standard material used as a road sub-base in Indian practice.

  Q: What is used as a road base course?
  A: WMM, governed by MoRTH Clause 406, is generally used as the base course above the sub-base, subject to the project's pavement design.

  Q: What is CBR in road construction?
  A: CBR (California Bearing Ratio) measures the load-bearing resistance of a compacted material relative to a reference crushed-stone standard, used to evaluate whether a pavement layer provides the support the design requires.

  Q: Why does grading matter for road base material?
  A: Grading controls density, load distribution and drainage behaviour once a layer is compacted. Both GSB and WMM are specified to grading envelopes for this reason, not supplied as a single loose aggregate size.

  Q: How is road aggregate tested?
  A: Common tests include sieve analysis (grading), CBR, Aggregate Impact Value, Los Angeles Abrasion, flakiness and elongation, plasticity index and moisture/compaction testing — which apply, and to what limits, depends on whether the material is GSB, WMM or another specified aggregate.

  Q: What should I check before buying road base material?
  A: Confirm the pavement layer, the project/tender specification, whether GSB, WMM or another graded aggregate applies, the required grading, testing/documentation needs, quantity, delivery location and schedule, and who is responsible for final blending or processing.

  Q: What information should I provide when requesting a quote?
  A: The material required (GSB, WMM aggregate or another graded aggregate), quantity and unit, project location, required grading, tender/BOQ specification, testing requirement, delivery date, site access constraints and documentation requirement.

  Q: Who is responsible for blending or mixing road base material?
  A: This depends on the project and contract — confirm explicitly whether the supplier or the contractor is responsible for final blending, mixing or processing before ordering, rather than assuming.

  Q: How much road base material do I need?
  A: Quantity is calculated from your project's layer area, thickness and design — share your BOQ or drawings and OM Group can work from that, once the specific material is identified.

  Q: Can OM Group supply multiple road materials on one order?
  A: Yes. GSB, WMM aggregate, graded aggregates, sand, boulders and Ready Mix Concrete can be quoted and coordinated together on a single procurement relationship.

  Q: What documentation should I request?
  A: Grading/sieve analysis, relevant physical test results and delivery documentation are the common requests — availability depends on the specific material, source and project requirement.

  Q: How much does road base material cost in Goa?
  A: There is no fixed published rate — price depends on which material (GSB, WMM aggregate or another graded aggregate), grading, quantity and delivery location. Share your requirement with OM Group for current pricing.

  A: Material type, grading, quantity, processing, source, transport distance, project location, current availability and project schedule.

  A: No. OM Group quotes against the specific material and requirement rather than publishing a fixed or "starting from" rate.

- [Washed Sand Supplier in Goa](https://www.omgroupco.com/products/washed-sand): OM GROUP supplies washed sand across North and South Goa, with current grading and specification information on request. Request a quote.

  Q: What is washed sand?
  A: Washed sand is sand that has undergone washing or washing-and-screening to remove unwanted fines and impurities, producing a cleaner, more controlled material.

  Q: What does washing sand do?
  A: Washing reduces the fine, low-value fraction in the sand and can improve grading consistency and overall cleanliness.

  Q: What does washing remove?
  A: Fine material and impurities from the sand's source — this can include crushing dust, clay, silt or organic matter, depending on the material. A controlled amount of fine material typically remains, since some fines are useful in a mix.

  Q: What is the relationship between washed sand and M-Sand?
  A: M-Sand describes a material — manufactured sand produced from crushed rock. Washed describes a process applied to sand. The exact relationship for the material OM Group supplies depends on the product in question; contact OM Group with your requirement for clarity on the specific material being supplied.

  Q: What is washed sand used for?
  A: Concrete, RCC, masonry and general construction, where the grading and specification suit the application.

  Q: Can washed sand be used for concrete?
  A: Yes, where the grading of the material suits the mix design.

  Q: Can washed sand be used for RCC?
  A: Yes, subject to the same grading and specification requirements as any fine aggregate used in reinforced concrete.

  Q: Can washed sand be used for RMC?
  A: Yes, where the material's grading matches the plant's mix design requirements.

  Q: Can washed sand be used for masonry?
  A: Yes, in mortar, where the project specification permits.

  Q: Can washed sand be used for plaster?
  A: Suitability for plaster depends on the specific grading of the material. A dedicated plaster-grade sand under IS 1542:1992 is generally specified for plastering work — confirm with your enquiry which specification your project needs.

  Q: What makes washed sand good quality?
  A: Consistent grading, controlled fines content, cleanliness from organic and deleterious material, and batch-to-batch consistency.

  Q: What grading does washed sand have?
  A: Grading is confirmed against current test data for the material being supplied.

  Q: Does washed sand contain fines?
  A: Yes — washing reduces fines rather than eliminating them entirely, since a controlled proportion of fine material is normal and useful in most mixes.

  Q: What is the difference between washed sand and river sand?
  A: River sand is a natural, water-deposited material; washing is a process that can be applied to natural sand or to other sand types to reduce fines and impurities. Whether OM Group's washed sand is river-sourced or otherwise depends on the specific material supplied.

  Q: Where can I buy washed sand in Goa?
  A: OM Group supplies washed sand across North and South Goa. Request a quote on this page or contact OM Group directly.

  Q: Does OM Group supply washed sand?
  A: Yes, across North and South Goa.

  Q: Can OM Group deliver washed sand across Goa?
  A: Yes, on OM Group's own transport fleet, with operational bases at Kundaim, Thivim and Sancoale.

  Q: What is the price of washed sand in Goa?
  A: Rate depends on quantity, delivery location, specification and schedule, so OM Group quotes against the specific requirement rather than publishing a list rate.

  Q: Is washed sand currently available?
  A: Availability is confirmed against the project requirement.

  Q: What specifications and documentation are available?
  A: Current grading and fines information can be provided on request, confirmed against the material being supplied.

  Q: How do I request a quote?
  A: Use the Request a Quote form with quantity, unit, application, project location and any grading requirement, or contact OM Group directly by phone or WhatsApp.

- [Wet Mix Macadam (WMM) Aggregate Supplier in Goa](https://www.omgroupco.com/products/wmm): OM GROUP supplies crushed, graded aggregate for Wet Mix Macadam (WMM) across Goa, matched to MoRTH Clause 406 and project specifications. Request a quote.

  Q: What is WMM?
  A: WMM (Wet Mix Macadam) is a pavement base-course material made by mechanically mixing clean, crushed, graded aggregate with controlled water in a wet mix plant, then compacting it into a dense layer, per MoRTH Clause 406.

  Q: What does WMM stand for?
  A: WMM stands for Wet Mix Macadam.

  Q: What is Wet Mix Macadam?
  A: Wet Mix Macadam is the full name for WMM — a crushed, graded aggregate blend, mixed with controlled water and compacted to form a pavement base course, specified under MoRTH Clause 406 and IRC:109.

  Q: What is WMM used for?
  A: WMM is used as the base course in flexible pavements for highways, roads, industrial and infrastructure projects, placed above the granular sub-base (GSB) and below the bituminous or surface layer.

  Q: Is WMM a base course?
  A: Yes. WMM is generally used as the base course, above the granular sub-base and below the bituminous or concrete surface, subject to the project's pavement design.

  Q: What grading does WMM require?
  A: WMM uses a single 0–53mm grading envelope per the applicable MoRTH table. Table numbering varies across sources and revisions, so the specific table and values should be verified against the applicable contract/MoRTH revision.

  Q: What is MoRTH Clause 406?
  A: MoRTH Clause 406, in Section 400 of the Specifications for Road and Bridge Works, is the principal Indian reference governing WMM production, grading and construction requirements.

  Q: What is IRC:109?
  A: IRC:109-2015 is the Indian Roads Congress guideline for Wet Mix Macadam, covering design and construction guidance alongside MoRTH Clause 406.

  Q: What is the Aggregate Impact Value requirement for WMM?
  A: A general standard requirement of ≤30% is cited under MoRTH Clause 406 — stricter than WBM. This is a specification reference, not an OM Group test result for a specific consignment.

  Q: What is the Los Angeles Abrasion requirement for WMM?
  A: A general standard requirement of ≤40% is cited under MoRTH Clause 406. This is a specification reference, not a claim about a specific tested consignment.

  Q: What is the flakiness and elongation requirement for WMM?
  A: A general standard requirement of ≤30% combined flakiness and elongation index is cited under MoRTH Clause 406.

  Q: What is the plasticity index requirement for WMM?
  A: A general standard requirement of ≤6, for the fraction passing 425 micron, is cited under MoRTH Clause 406.

  Q: What is WMM layer thickness?
  A: A single compacted WMM layer is generally not less than 75mm, and up to 200mm with vibratory compaction, per Clause 406 — confirm against the project's pavement design.

  Q: How is WMM compacted?
  A: WMM is compacted after mixing and spreading, with lateral confinement during laying and moisture controlled near the Optimum Moisture Content (OMC) determined per IS 2720 Part 8.

  Q: Why is moisture control important in WMM?
  A: Moisture content close to OMC is what allows the material to reach its target compacted density — placement too wet or too dry of OMC falls short of the density the pavement design assumes, regardless of grading quality.

  Q: What is the difference between WMM and GSB?
  A: GSB is the sub-base layer, governed by MoRTH Clause 401; WMM is the base course above it, governed by Clause 406, more rigorously graded and plant-mixed with controlled moisture. They are not interchangeable.

  Q: Is WMM the same as WBM?
  A: No. WBM (Water Bound Macadam) is the older on-site binding method; WMM is plant-mixed with controlled moisture and forced mixing, and carries a stricter Aggregate Impact Value limit.

  Q: Is crusher-run the same as WMM?
  A: No. Crusher-run is an uncontrolled mixed-size crusher output. WMM requires controlled proportioning to the specified grading envelope and controlled moisture mixing — crusher-run does not by itself establish compliance with the WMM specification.

  Q: Is WMM the same as 40mm aggregate?
  A: No. 40mm aggregate is one crushed fraction — an input to a WMM blend, not WMM itself. WMM is a blend proportioned to a 0–53mm grading curve, not a single size.

  Q: Can GSB replace WMM?
  A: No. GSB and WMM occupy different, specified positions in the pavement structure, governed by different MoRTH clauses. One cannot be substituted for the other without engineering approval.

  Q: Can crusher-run replace WMM?
  A: Not as supplied. Crusher-run must first be proportioned to the Clause 406 grading and mixed with controlled moisture before it meets the WMM specification.

  Q: Where can I buy WMM aggregate in Goa?
  A: OM Group supplies WMM aggregate across North and South Goa, produced at its own crushing operation. Request a quote on this page or contact OM Group directly.

  Q: Who supplies WMM aggregate in Goa?
  A: OM Group supplies the crushed, graded aggregate fractions used in WMM production across Goa, as part of its road and infrastructure materials range.

  Q: What information is needed for a WMM aggregate quote?
  A: Project location, required quantity, required grading, applicable MoRTH revision/contract specification, aggregate fractions required, delivery schedule and any documentation requirement.

  Q: Can OM Group supply bulk quantities?
  A: Yes. OM Group supplies aggregate at project volumes and operates its own transport fleet for dispatch across Goa.

  Q: Can OM Group provide WMM specification information?
  A: Yes. Grading and general specification reference information is available on request, confirmed against the applicable project and MoRTH revision.

  Q: Can OM Group provide WMM aggregate test documentation?
  A: Where current test data exists for the specific material and project, it is provided on request. Not every parameter is tested for every shipment.

  Q: What affects WMM aggregate pricing?
  A: Quantity, grading requirement, delivery location and transport distance, documentation requirements, current availability and project schedule.

  Q: Does OM Group manufacture WMM?
  A: OM Group supplies the crushed, graded aggregate used in WMM production, produced at its own crushing operation and matched to the applicable specification. OM Group does not currently claim to operate a wet mix plant or supply ready-to-lay WMM material.

  Q: Does OM Group supply aggregate for WMM?
  A: Yes. 40mm, 20mm, 10mm, 6mm and screenings — the fractions a WMM blend requires — are part of OM Group's crushed stone aggregate range.

  Q: Where does OM Group supply WMM aggregate in Goa?
  A: Across North and South Goa, dispatched from OM Group's own transport bases at Kundaim, Thivim and Sancoale.

  Q: Can OM Group supply different aggregate fractions for WMM?
  A: Yes. OM Group's crushing operation produces multiple nominal sizes, so the fractions a WMM blend requires can be supplied together or coordinated by proportion.

  Q: Does OM Group supply WMM aggregate in North Goa?
  A: Yes, WMM aggregate is supplied across North Goa.

  Q: Does OM Group supply WMM aggregate in South Goa?
  A: Yes, WMM aggregate is supplied across South Goa.
